newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Taiwan sees Central America trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sees Central America trade pact.

text.p: Taiwan plans to sign a free trade pact with various nations in Central America, aiming to bump up trade with the region, a Taiwanese diplomat said on Tuesday.
"The Central American countries have formed a common market, which has made the region more attractive," Rafael Wang, spokesman for the Taiwanese embassay in Honduras, said.
He said the accord would be signed in September and would include Belize, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama.
Wang said that Taiwan is also planning to create an economic development fund to support the seven Central American countries in the pact.
The Central American nations are also negotiating free trade deals with Mexico and plan to propose one to the United States when President Bill Clinton visits Costa Rica later in the year.
They are looking for free trade pacts with other trading groups.
